_readme: tools/eval_board.py's expectations against 'chain all' (R2). Each entry: 'stage' (a list of chain-test stage numbers), an optional 'match' (field->value, or field->[allowed values], to pick which @S<stage>.<n> result lines within those stages this entry judges), 'check' (one of 'verdict', 'field_eq', 'field_max', 'field_min', 'field_in') with 'value' (or 'field'+'value' for the field_* checks), 'source' ('run19': measured on silicon, checked against BOTH A and B; 'prediction': about the NEXT run only, checked against B only), 'date' (the docs/HARDWARE-LOG.md entry this came from), and 'note' (kept in the deviation line). Field names match chaintest.c's own @S<stage>.<n> lines verbatim (ksps, overrun, late, missed, load_max_x10, ...). Update this file only from a confirmed board run (BR.9), tagging new/changed entries with that run's number - see board-run-task.md section 6 and 10.

expectations.note: run 19: 8 MSPS for 15 s, 120000509 transfers, overrun 0, late 0, missed 0, isr = half + done
run 19: S5 triangle grid clean (slip 0.03-0.09 samples), slope/model 1.000 at 100 kSPS, 1/4/8/10 MSPS
run 19: S4 at 10 MSPS showed overrun 732 of 0.5M transfers - a known limit of this silicon, not a fault; reported here only so a silent change (better or worse) is not dropped
run 19: S5 at 16/20 MSPS lost triggers (slip 6.2/5.0 samples) - the triangle FAIL there is the known limit, not a new fault
predicted after run 19 (processing-loop rewrite, tolerance fixes): S4 and S6 pass at 1, 4 and 8 MSPS
predicted after run 19: S9 ("the attempt") picks 8 or 10 MSPS as the rate that streams cleanly
predicted after run 19 (unrolled 32-bit processing loop): processing load at 8 MSPS falls well below half (was 92% = load_max_x10 920 in run 19)
